title: Storage: disk, volumes and what persists
standfirst: “Persistent” can mean the whole disk, one mounted folder, or fourteen days. It can also mean a separate volume that outlives the machine, which is a different product from the disk the machine boots with.
idea: There are three storage objects in this market. The root disk is part of the machine and disappears or is parked with it. A volume is a separate disk you attach, which can outlive the machine and sometimes attach to another. Object storage is a bucket reached over the network, not a filesystem.

What persists is the second question. Some providers keep the whole filesystem, including packages installed outside the home directory. Others keep one folder, usually /workspace or /data, and reset the rest from the template. The difference shows up the first time you install a database in /var/lib.

Retention is the third. A stopped machine's disk may be kept indefinitely, kept free for a fixed period, or deleted with the machine. A volume may be node-local and lost with the host. Read the retention line before treating a sandbox as storage.

splits.heading: The whole disk, or one folder
body: Agent 37, boxd, Boat and Sprites persist the whole disk. Lizard persists only /workspace unless you pause rather than stop, and InstaBox gives you one disk at /data with the root disk owned by the template. E2B's snapshots cover the filesystem, but its separate volumes are the object that outlives a sandbox.
The narrow case is easy to miss because the marketing says “persistent”. At Lizard, a stop deletes everything outside /workspace; only a pause keeps the installed packages.

splits.heading: Volumes are a separate product
body: Runtime attaches up to four volumes per sandbox, and a volume can also be mounted read-only as a snapshot. Blaxel allows one volume per sandbox, attached to one sandbox at a time, and sells Agent Drive for shared access. Vercel's drives allow one read-write mount at a time. Morph's volumes are S3-compatible object storage, not an attached block disk.
Several providers have no volume product at all: Agent 37, Boat, Sandboxer and InstaBox. E2B's volumes exist but are in private beta.

splits.heading: Retention is where “persistent” ends
body: Boat keeps a stopped sandbox's disk for 14 days, then deletes it. Lizard's volumes are node-local, and there is no trash: deleting a sandbox or a project removes its data at once. Vercel's snapshots expire after 30 days by default unless you remove the expiry.
Agent 37 keeps the disk until you delete the instance, and charges $0.09 per GB-month for it. Sprites caps storage at 100 GB per Sprite and bills the bytes you write.

watchFor: Whether the whole filesystem survives or only one mounted folder.
Whether a volume can attach to more than one machine, and whether sharing is read-only.
How long a stopped machine's disk is kept before deletion.
Whether storage bills on provisioned size or written bytes.
Whether snapshots include credentials and installed packages outside the home folder.

rows.scenario: The whole disk persists and bills until you delete the instance, but the nightly backup covers only /home/node, so the database is not in it.
rows.note: The whole disk persists and bills at $0.09 per GB-month until you delete the instance. No volumes. Backups cover only /home/node, so a database in /var/lib is not in them.

rows.scenario: The sandbox disk goes with the sandbox; only a volume survives deletion, and one volume attaches at a time.
rows.note: A volume survives sandbox deletion, but only one volume attaches to a sandbox and a volume attaches to one sandbox at a time. Agent Drive is the shared filesystem, priced separately.

source.quote: you can only attach one volume to a sandbox. A volume can also only be attached to one sandbox at a time.

rows.scenario: The whole disk persists, including /var/lib, and is kept free for 14 days after a stop.
rows.note: The whole disk persists, with 51 GB on the smaller sizes and no volume product. A stopped sandbox's disk is kept free for 14 days, then deleted.

source.quote: boat keeps the disk for 14 days after the stop

rows.scenario: The fixed 100 GB disk persists in every state and bills on bytes written, not provisioned size.
rows.note: Every machine has a fixed 100 GB disk, and disk bills on bytes written in every state. Separate disks now have a guide: they outlive the machine they are attached to, and attach to one machine at a time.

rows.scenario: Postgres in /var/lib is gone when the instance stops; only a snapshot or a mounted R2 bucket keeps the data.
rows.note: 20 GB maximum disk, deleted when the instance stops. A snapshot keeps the root filesystem for 30 days; an R2 directory backup or S3/R2 mount outlives every instance.

source.quote: Stopping the instance deletes the files on its disk.

rows.scenario: Postgres in /var/lib survives a stop because the whole disk persists, but it bills while stopped and cannot exceed 10 GiB.
rows.note: The whole disk persists and bills in stopped and paused states at $0.000108/GiB-hour. Volumes are S3-backed FUSE mounts, 100 per organisation, free, and not usable for block storage such as database tables.

source.quote: Daytona volumes are included at no additional cost. Each organization can create up to 100 volumes, and volume data does not count against your storage quota.

rows.scenario: Snapshots keep the filesystem, but the sandbox disk does not outlive the sandbox; separate volumes are in private beta.
rows.note: Snapshots keep the filesystem, and separate volumes persist across sandboxes, but volumes are in private beta and cannot be snapshotted. Included disk is 10 GiB on Hobby and 20 GiB on Pro.

source.quote: Disk | Included (10 GiB Hobby / 20 GiB Pro)

rows.scenario: One disk at /data persists and grows live; the root disk is owned by the template, so a package install outside /data is at risk.
rows.note: One disk at /data, 20 GiB by default and growable, with the root disk owned by the template. No volumes and no second disk; the free plan's disk is fixed.

source.quote: a 20 GiB persistent ext4 disk at `/data`

rows.scenario: Only /workspace persists; a stop deletes everything else, including the database in /var/lib.
rows.note: The local disk is lost on stop; only /workspace persists, through a named volume of 1–50 GB attached to one sandbox at a time and stored on one node. There is no trash.

source.quote: New volumes allow **1 to 50 GB**, in whole GB, with **5 GB** as the default.

rows.scenario: The database lives on the fixed 512 GiB root disk, which cannot be resized and is billed as memory at 20:1; a Volume is the durable option.
rows.note: A fixed 512 GiB root filesystem, not resizable, billed by raising the memory request at a 20:1 ratio. Volumes are separate, survive the sandbox, are excluded from snapshots, and cost $0.09/GiB-month after 1 TiB.

source.quote: On the VM runtime, the root filesystem is a fixed 512 GiB.

rows.scenario: The instance disk holds the machine; Morph Volumes is S3-compatible object storage reached through a gateway, not an attached block disk.
rows.note: The instance disk holds the machine, and Morph Volumes is separate S3-compatible object storage reached through a gateway and CLI, not an attached block disk. EFS is a third option.

source.quote: Morph Volumes are persistent S3-compatible storage for build caches, release artifacts, checkpoints, and shared datasets.

rows.scenario: Up to four volumes mount at chosen paths, so the database belongs on a volume rather than the root disk.
rows.note: Up to four volumes per sandbox, each mounted at a path, with a read-only snapshot mode for sharing. Buckets from S3, R2 or GCS can appear as a directory without the key entering the sandbox.

source.quote: A create attaches up to four volumes, each at a path such as `/data`

rows.scenario: The whole disk persists while stopped, free within a storage quota; going over blocks new sandboxes rather than charging.
rows.note: The whole disk persists while stopped, free within a storage quota, and there is no separate volume or image registry. Going over quota blocks new sandboxes rather than charging.

source.quote: is space for your files, added on top of the OS image

rows.scenario: The whole filesystem persists on durable local storage, capped at 100 GB, and bills the bytes written.
rows.note: The whole filesystem persists on durable local storage, capped at 100 GB, and checkpoints keep filesystem blocks that bill while retained. No attachable or shared volumes are documented.

source.quote: you pay for the bytes you actually write, not the full 100 GB

rows.scenario: 64 GB of ephemeral NVMe per sandbox; a drive bills on logical used size and only one sandbox can mount it read-write.
rows.note: 64 GB of ephemeral NVMe per sandbox, plus drives billed on logical used size. Only one sandbox at a time can mount a drive read-write; snapshots are the sharing mechanism.

rows.scenario: The root disk is ephemeral, so anything that must outlive the sandbox goes on a mounted volume or a hosted Git repository.
rows.note: Root disk 10–100 GB, ephemeral and growth-only. Cloud Volumes mount as ordinary POSIX directories, are durable and versioned with snapshots and time travel, and up to 8 can be mounted per sandbox, read-only, prefetched or pinned to a snapshot. Hosted Git repositories mount without a clone.

source.quote: The sandbox's root disk is ephemeral; a mounted filesystem is durable, survives the sandbox, and can be shared by many sandboxes at once.

rows.scenario: Postgres in /var/lib survives a power-off and a reboot, and a volume can outlive the Droplet.
rows.note: The whole boot disk persists with the machine. Volumes run from 1 GiB to 16 TiB at $0.10/GiB-month and attach to one Droplet at a time. Volumes are billed whether attached or not, and are not included in Droplet backups.

source.quote: DigitalOcean Volumes Block Storage cost $0.10 per GiB per month and range from 1 GiB to 16384 GiB (16 TiB).

rows.scenario: The 20 GiB the agent writes lives on the plan disk and is still there next session, because the disk is never thrown away while the server exists.
rows.note: The whole disk persists and is billed whether or not the server runs. Extra storage is a volume at €0.044 per GB a month, up to 10 TB and 16 volumes per server, but a volume attaches to only one server at a time. Object Storage is S3-compatible with no native mount.

source.quote: We will bill you for your servers until you delete them, independent of their state.

figureLabel: Disk, and how long it is kept

scenario.title: Install Postgres in /var/lib, stop overnight
scenario.setup: The agent installs Postgres with apt, initialises a database in /var/lib/postgresql, and writes a week of test data. You stop the machine at 22:00 and resume at 08:00.

beats.what: apt install writes outside the home folder, which is where the whole-disk and one-folder designs diverge.
Stop. The disk is either kept with the machine, parked for a fixed period, or deleted.
Resume and start Postgres. If the disk was reset to the template, the database is gone and the install has to run again.

scenario.turn: A provider that persists the whole disk keeps the database; one that persists only /workspace or a single /data disk does not, and one that wipes the disk on stop loses it entirely. Retention is the second half: a 14-day window turns a long weekend into data loss.

questions: Does the whole filesystem survive a stop, or only /workspace or /data, and what resets from the template?
How long is a stopped machine's disk kept before deletion, and is that in the docs or only in the terms?
Does storage bill on provisioned capacity, written bytes or used bytes, and does a paused machine still pay for it?
Can a volume attach to more than one machine, and is sharing read-only?
Do snapshots include packages installed outside the home folder, and do they carry saved credentials?
